senses.gloss: Rāta (BL), modification of or mistake for Rāvata or Rāuta.
rati, ratī (IE 8-8; IA 19), also spelt rattī; a small weight; see Sanskrit raktikā.
rati , same as raktikā; a little above 1(3/4) grains.

ratna (IE 7-1-2), ‘five’; sometimes also used to indicate ‘nine’, and rarely even ‘fourteen’.
 (EI 22; CII 4), same as the Buddhist tri-ratna, i. e. the Buddha, Dharma and Saṅgha.
 (ML), a relic [of the Buddha].

ratna-gṛha (CII 3), ‘the jewel-house’; the house enshrining the three ratṅas, regarded by some as denoting a great Buddhist stūpa.
 (EI 19; LL), Buddhist; a sanctuary; the sanctuary of a Buddha image.

ratna-traya (EI 8), Jain; samyag-darśana, samyag-jñāna and samyak-cāritra.
 (EI 27, 30, 31), Buddhist; the tri-ratna or trinity; a Buddhist religious establishment enshrining the three ratnas; rent-free land in its possession (Ep. Ind., Vol. XXX, p. 46). Cf. ratnatraya-sambhoga.

ratnatraya-sambhoga (HRS), traced in Bengal records; rent-free holding in the possession of Buddhist religious establishments where the Buddha, Dharma and Saṅgha were worshipped; same as ratna-traya. Cf. rāja-sambhoga.
